claims.text: Pre-oxidation at approximately 600°C for about 1 hour in an oxygen-rich atmosphere will form a thin, uniform, adherent B2O3 surface layer on boride-based components.
The resulting B2O3 layer will be sub-micron in thickness.
A preformed B2O3 layer will reduce direct reaction between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
The B2O3 layer acts as a thin, dense physical and chemical barrier.
The B2O3 barrier reduces aluminum diffusion into the boride substrate.
Reduced aluminum diffusion limits corrosive reactions at the substrate–melt interface.
The ceramic-like B2O3 layer hinders the transport of aluminum ions.
Hindered aluminum transport reduces the kinetics of corrosive interfacial reactions.
Pre-oxidized components will have lower weight loss than untreated components after molten-aluminum exposure.
Pre-oxidized components will exhibit less pitting than untreated components after molten-aluminum exposure.
Pre-oxidized components will retain greater microstructural integrity than untreated components after molten-aluminum exposure.
The intervention should remain effective during exposure to molten aluminum at approximately 700–750°C for up to 48 hours.
Mechanical or thermal disruption of the oxide scale may reduce its protective durability.
A non-uniform or poorly adherent oxide layer may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
Untreated boride-based components without pre-oxidation are the standard components currently used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
